_instructions: Copy this file to <project root>/local.settings.json (gitignored) and fill it in.
There is NO fixed schema. Every key below is named by your own manage-deployments.js
target config -- scriptIdKey / deploymentIdKey / sheetIdKey / authKey. Rename freely;
what matters is that the *Key values and this file agree. See the package README
section 'local.settings.json'.
scriptId        - the Apps Script project ID, matching each target's scriptIdKey. Two
targets may point at the same key when one script project holds both
named deployments.
claspAuth       - the clasp credential file (a `clasp login --creds` output) this project
deploys with, matching authKey (default 'claspAuth', settable per target).
Without it clasp silently falls back to ~/.clasprc.json, which may be a
different Google account that cannot see this project's deployments.
Confirm which account can, rather than assuming:
clasp_config_auth=<candidate file> clasp deployments
*DeploymentId   - matching each target's deploymentIdKey. DO NOT hand-populate: the package
writes it after every deploy, and the resolver validates it against the
live list before reusing it. Reserve the key name and leave it out.
*SheetId        - matching each target's sheetIdKey. Optional: an unset key prints
'(<key> not set in local.settings.json)' in the deploy summary rather
than a broken URL.
Project-specific keys (a static-host repo path for gas-static, an admin secret, an API
token) live in this same file. The package reads only the keys its config names.
CANONICAL KEYS -- the same fact gets the same key in every project, camelCase, never
SCREAMING_CASE. Prefer these over a project-local spelling; see the README section
'Canonical keys'. claspAuth, scriptId, deploymentId, adminSecret, staticRepoPath,
sheetId / docId, gasLogDir / gasLogFolderId / gasLogPrefix, axiomDataset / axiomToken /
axiomQueryToken.
1. Env-scoping is structural, not a prefix: a fact that varies per environment is
written once per environment; a project-wide fact is written once.
2. Project-specific keys are fine as long as they do not restate a canonical concept.
A fourth spelling of 'the static repo' is not configurability, it is drift.
The *Key indirection below is how an unmigrated project keeps working -- a legacy
override, not the normal way to configure a new project. Which of these live in a
committed gas-project.json rather than here is settled by GAS-Core adr/0002.
